clue.text: Military group's lack of involvement

definitions.meaning: a unit of troops sent away from the main body on a special task

explanation.surface: An army unit is accused of keeping out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a squad posted apart from its regiment and a cool, uninvolved aloofness.

clue.text: It's a fact lawyer's taken on corporation

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
corporation is an old jokey word for a big belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that an attorney has joined a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is the old slang for a paunch, hence TUM; 'taken on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item of information, a given, is a datum.

clue.text: Restaurant serving up a pastry dish, being without things like doughnuts?

indicators.note: being without means standing outside, so the turned-round piece wraps the other
in a down clue 'up' tells us the words a tart are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tart is a dish made with pastry
tori, plural of torus, are ring shapes like doughnuts

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves a tart but has run out of doughnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' turns the dish round (it is a down clue), and 'being without' means standing outside the doughnut shapes, not lacking them.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eating house, typically informal, is a trattoria.

clue.text: Self-assured individual and friend meet privately

parts.note: self-assured means confident
I is one, an individual
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A confident person and a pal get together in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in confidence, off the record, is speaking privately.

clue.text: Dicky, Norm, Des — trendy types?

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the two names are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of three men's names, Dicky, Norm and Des, asked whether they are fashionable sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a third name in the list but is the anagram signal (British slang for weak or faulty).
explanation.definitionFit: Up-to-date, fashionable people are moderns.

clue.text: Person scoring a century is caught by him, presumably

indicators.note: being caught by something means held inside it, so the hundred goes into the phrase

parts.note: a male person is presumably not a woman, so him gives the phrase not her
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A batsman reaching a hundred is caught out by a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a batsman caught on a hundred misleads; 'him, presumably' is a man, so not a woman. To notch is to score, keeping a tally with cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: One who keeps a tally by cutting marks, or scores points, is a notcher.

clue.text: Inventor included in Nobel lists

indicators.note: included in signals that the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

explanation.surface: An inventor appears on the Nobel prize lists.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Graham Bell, the telephone pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with patenting the telephone, a famous example of an inventor.

clue.text: Banishment Exodus passage recorded?

indicators.note: something recorded is put on tape to be heard played back, so we listen to the words

parts.note: Ex is the abbreviation of the Bible book Exodus, and an aisle is a passage

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the biblical expulsion is written in Exodus.
explanation.walkthrough: EX (Exodus) plus AISLE (passage), said out loud, give the answer; 'passage' misleads as a stretch of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent away from one's homeland is exile.

clue.text: Lass more distressed, having invested a thousand in failing enterprise

indicators.note: investing puts money in, so the thousand goes inside the scrambled letters
distressed means battered or upset, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: An upset girl has sunk a thousand into a business going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges LASS MORE, and 'having invested' puts K inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that runs at a loss, failing to profit, is a loss-maker.

clue.text: As player of music, a solo presenter, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A one-person radio host is offered as a music player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A SOLO PRESENTER; a solo presenter is also what the device is, playing music to one listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walkman-style portable cassette or CD player with headphones was called this.

clue.text: Given guidance in trade organisation

indicators.note: organisation means putting into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been coached within a trade body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like a trade body, but it signals the rearranging of IN TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled or coached has been trained.

clue.text: Fashionable birds going round awful place

indicators.note: going round means the birds surround the fashionable word

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
hep is dated slang for fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Trendy birds circling a dreadful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for the worst place or situation imaginable.

clue.text: Old woman's protest about court case being cut short

indicators.note: about means the protest goes around the shortened word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a trial is a court case

explanation.surface: An old woman's demonstration over a trial that ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is not an elderly lady here but a family's female head; 'being cut short' drops the court case's last letter before 'about' wraps the protest round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The female head of a family, often elderly, is its matriarch.

clue.text: Energy shown by school's first XI

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word school's

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A school's first eleven shows great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour or drive, as in 'running out of puff', is called steam.

clue.text: Swell-sounding fabric

indicators.note: sounding means we hear a word spelt differently

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea

explanation.surface: A cloth that sounds lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as an adjective meaning splendid, but it is the noun, a surge of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth used for suits is serge.

clue.text: Slave has fight with famous Roman, losing it

parts.note: to spar is to fight

indicators.note: losing means the next word is taken out of the name

parts.note: Tacitus was a famous Roman historian
taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: A slave fights a famous Roman and is defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing it' takes IT out of TACITUS to leave TACUS. Spartacus led a slave revolt against Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator, a slave, who led a rising against Rome.

clue.text: Animal born after early part of year, right?

indicators.note: after puts the born letter behind the season

parts.note: spring is the early part of the year
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Asking if a creature born in spring is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African gazelle, the springbok, is a kind of antelope.

clue.text: Rock hit's sound enthralling husband

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the husband goes inside

parts.note: bats means hits, as with a bat
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A hit record's tune captivating a married man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' puts H inside BATSTONE; Bath stone is a building limestone from around the English city of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream limestone quarried near Bath, used in building, is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Group of countries led by a mostly evil princess

indicators.note: led by puts the continent after the first two pieces
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: nasty means evil
Asia is a continent, a group of countries

explanation.surface: A nation-bloc headed by a wicked royal daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NASTY to NAST. Anastasia was the youngest daughter of the last Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Duchess Anastasia of Russia is a famous example of a princess.

clue.text: Rose, for example, after second request

indicators.note: after puts the request behind the second

parts.note: a prayer is a request

explanation.surface: A rose bush follows a second plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' is not the flower but the perforated nozzle of a watering can.
explanation.definitionFit: The perforated nozzle of a watering can, its rose, scatters water as a fine spray.

clue.text: American in detached state

parts.note: a citizen of the US state separated from the rest of the country by Canada

explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the US state cut off from the other mainland states, so its native is one of these.

clue.text: Off-putting response to suggestion

parts.note: a reply that puts the idea off until another time

explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not now, some other time' postpones, literally puts off, a proposal.

clue.text: What beats, say, an Indian dish?

indicators.note: say means pronounce, so we hear a sound-alike

parts.note: the heart, which beats, is slang a ticker

explanation.surface: Asking what tops an Indian curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats' reads as defeats, but it is the heart beating; ticker is slang for heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Marinated pieces of meat cooked in a tandoor, as in chicken tikka, form a curry-house dish.

clue.text: Strong paper boat's sound

indicators.note: sound tells us to hear the word, not read it

parts.note: a craft is a boat

explanation.surface: Tough paper with the noise of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough brown wrapping paper made from sulphate pulp is called kraft.

clue.text: Does start badly in trials

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A deer gets off to a poor start in competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb but works as plain letters; 'badly' rearranges DOES START.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial runs of a vehicle or product in real use are these tests.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom female scholar discovered

parts.note: she is a female
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: An old realm found by a woman academic.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land ruled by the queen who visited Solomon was an old realm.

clue.text: Sussex town infested with insects, we've heard

indicators.note: we've heard means the word is listened to, not read

parts.note: creepy-crawly, swarming with bugs, gives crawly

explanation.surface: A Sussex town reported to be full of bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Crawley is a town in West Sussex, by Gatwick airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawley is a large new town in West Sussex, England.

clue.text: One's performance in party given record backing

definitions.text: One's performance in party given record backing

parts.words: One's performance in party given record backing
parts.note: an amateur singing at a party over a recorded backing track

explanation.definitionFit: A pub or party entertainment where people sing along to recorded instrumentals.

clue.text: Place to take exams, originally

annotationWithheld.why: Place to take exams, originally (4): only parse is SIT (to take exams) + E (exams, originally), with 'exams' doing two jobs

clue.text: Organ padre restored for musical performance

indicators.note: restored means put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A church organ is repaired by a priest for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges ORGAN PADRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully sung opera on a serious theme, with no spoken dialogue, is this genre.
